answer: Cross-cluster quorum admission requires a candidate agent to collect one signed quartz from a verifier on each of three disjoint routing trees before claiming a task knoll. Issuing its $k$-th active quartz to entrants trailing the same upstream liquidity source forces a verifier to forfeit $10k$ cedar of its own routing yield to the protocol sink. An honest entrant with independent backing costs its three verifiers 30 cedar total, whereas an operator registering $m$ clones from one liquidity pool must bribe verifiers to forfeit $15m(m+1)$ cedar of yield across the three trees.
